gate: L1(d) — production DB is PROVABLY non-pausing
chosen_host: Postgres inside the existing Docker stack (docker-compose.yml:12-26), per the P0-014 decision
rule: Control-plane status is never evidence. On 2026-09-03 get_project returned ACTIVE_HEALTHY while execute_sql returned 28P01 and get_advisors said the project was hibernated.

assumption_to_confirm.claim: the old Supabase tier pauses after ~7 days of inactivity
assumption_to_confirm.status: UNVERIFIED by the CEO — stated in Supabase's own docs, not measured here
assumption_to_confirm.handling: the idle window below is set to >= 7 days so the proof holds whether the real threshold is 1 day or 7; founder can confirm the exact number from the dashboard, it only ever shortens the wait

proofs.name: ordered idle-window test
proofs.what: Stand up the production Postgres, write a marker row, then leave the stack completely untouched for a documented idle window of >= 7 days (no queries, no deploys, no health-check traffic against the DB). At the end, run a real query.
proofs.pass_criteria: the query returns the marker row on the FIRST attempt, with no wake-up latency and no error; raw psql output + timestamps recorded
records: wall-clock latency of the first query
docker container uptime across the window
proofs.why_first_attempt_matters: a paused host also answers eventually — 'wakes on next supported request' is exactly what the Supabase advisor said. The failure signature is a first request that errors or stalls, so only the FIRST attempt is evidence.
proofs.practicality: cheap but slow: it costs nothing but calendar time and can run in parallel with the rest of the pre-launch work, provided nobody touches the box. Start it the day the host exists.

proofs.name: structural evidence
proofs.what: Record that the chosen host has no pause mechanism to begin with: postgres:16-alpine has no inactivity-suspend feature, the service is declared restart: unless-stopped, and no managed control plane can suspend it.
proofs.pass_criteria: docker-compose.yml:12-26 cited + `docker inspect` showing RestartPolicy=unless-stopped + no scheduler/cron on the host that stops the container
proofs.honest_limit: This is an argument from the absence of a feature. It is strong, but it is not a measurement — it does NOT replace P1, it explains why P1 is expected to pass.

proofs.name: the risk that REPLACED pausing (CEO addition, not in the order)
proofs.why: Self-hosting removes auto-pause and puts three different failure modes in its place. A gate that only proves 'it does not pause' would declare victory against last week's failure while the same 4am outage arrives by another route.

modes.proof: container comes back automatically — reboot the host once, confirm the stack is up and answering with no manual step, record the exit code

modes.mode: disk full (backups accumulate on the same volume)
modes.proof: disk alerting exists and fires below 100% — this is gate (c), and it is why gate (b) requires off-host backup copies
restart policy plus an alert on repeated restarts; a container that restarts every 30s is 'up' to Docker and down to customers

proofs.recommendation: fold P3 into gate (c) alerting rather than tracking it separately — same alerting channel, same launch gate

what_would_make_this_gate_fake: accepting a control-plane/dashboard status instead of a query result — the exact P0-014 mistake
running the P1 query more than once and reporting the successful retry — the first attempt IS the measurement
any traffic touching the DB during the idle window (a health check, a cron, an idle Prisma pool keepalive) — it invalidates the window; record what was stopped
proving P2 only, and calling the gate met — absence of a pause feature is an argument, not a measurement
status: designed 2026-09-04; NOT executed — the production host does not exist yet (P0-017). P1 starts the day it does.
